title: Dhanush's 'Kara' Hits Netflix on May 28. The Box Office Was Disappointing. The Streaming Second Life Might Not Be.
excerpt: The ₹100 crore Tamil heist thriller underperformed theatrically with just ₹41 crore worldwide. Now Netflix is betting that Dhanush's star power and the film's raw action sequences will find a bigger audience at home.
body:
Dhanush doesn't make small films. Even when they underperform, they arrive with ambition, a ₹100 crore budget, and the kind of raw physicality that makes his peers look like they're acting in slow motion.

*Kara* — his heist-action thriller set in 1991 Ramanathapuram during the Gulf War — released theatrically on April 30 to mixed reviews and disappointing box office numbers. It earned roughly ₹41 crore worldwide against a ₹100 crore budget. By any commercial metric, that's a loss.

But Netflix has acquired the post-theatrical streaming rights, and *Kara* hits the platform on May 28. The film's second life starts in five days.

## What 'Kara' Is Actually About

Directed by Vignesh Raja and co-written with Alfred Prakash, *Kara* follows Karasaami — a reformed thief who gets pulled back into crime after his family's ancestral land is seized by a corrupt bank. The setting is specific and atmospheric: rural Tamil Nadu in the early '90s, a period when the Gulf War disrupted the livelihoods of thousands of families dependent on remittances from the Middle East.

It's a revenge heist film wrapped in a period drama, with Dhanush doing what Dhanush does best — channelling quiet fury into explosive action. Mamitha Baiju plays opposite him, and K. S. Ravikumar appears in a supporting role.

Critics were divided. The action sequences were praised as some of the most intense in recent Tamil cinema. The pacing and narrative structure drew complaints. The audience response, however, was more generous — those who saw it in theatres largely enjoyed the visceral, no-frills filmmaking.

## Why Streaming Could Save It

The theatrical economics of Tamil cinema are increasingly unforgiving. *Kara* had to compete with a crowded release calendar, limited international screens, and the reality that many NRI viewers simply don't have access to Tamil-language theatrical releases in their cities.

Netflix changes that equation entirely. The film will be available globally from May 28 in Tamil, Telugu, and potentially other dubbed languages. For the Indian diaspora — particularly in the US, UK, Canada, and the Middle East — this is the real release.

Dhanush is one of the rare Tamil actors whose name alone drives clicks on streaming platforms. *The Gray Man* introduced him to Western audiences. *Thiruchitrambalam* was a JioHotstar hit. Netflix knows his name translates to viewership numbers in a way that most regional Indian stars don't.

## The OTT Economics

The streaming rights deal for *Kara* was reportedly locked before the theatrical release, which is standard practice for big-budget Tamil films. Netflix likely paid a premium for Dhanush's involvement — and the theatrical underperformance actually works in the platform's favour. Audiences who skipped the theatre will now discover the film at home, giving Netflix a "fresh" release rather than day-and-date competition.

This is the new model for Indian cinema: theatrical as marketing, streaming as distribution. A ₹41 crore theatrical run isn't a failure if the streaming deal already recovered a significant portion of the budget. The real question is whether *Kara* generates the kind of viewing numbers on Netflix that justify future Dhanush acquisitions at similar price points.

## What NRIs Should Know

If you missed *Kara* in theatres — and statistically, most of you did — May 28 is your window. The film works best as a lean, violent, atmosphere-heavy thriller. Don't go in expecting *Raanjhanaa* or *Asuran*. This is Dhanush in action-star mode, carrying a film on physical performance and screen presence.

Stream it in Tamil if you can. The dialogue has a specificity to the Ramanathapuram landscape that dubbed versions won't fully capture.

## Dhanush's Loaded 2026

*Kara* is just one piece of Dhanush's absurdly packed year. He has *D55* (a socially conscious action drama), a biopic on former President APJ Abdul Kalam, and an Ilaiyaraaja biopic all in various stages of production. The man is working at a pace that would exhaust actors half his age.

*Kara* streams on Netflix from May 28, 2026. Set a reminder.
nri_angle: For NRIs who couldn't catch Kara in its limited US/UK theatrical run — or who live outside the major metro areas where Tamil films get screens — Netflix is the second chance. Dhanush is one of the few Tamil actors with genuine global streaming pull, and Kara's availability in Tamil, Telugu, and other languages makes it accessible across the diaspora's linguistic spectrum.
author: Diaspora Desk
